take_homes: Licences rolled out are not adoption. If someone reports access as use, I ask who is actually using it, for what, and instead of what.
No named owner means it isn't real. Before any AI plan reaches me, I ask who answers for it.
The comparison is always against what people do today (the spreadsheet, the colleague, the gut call). A case that doesn't beat that fails.

monday.move: Ask the controller who would own the month-end variance commentary if an agent drafted it, and how long it takes today. That is the baseline and the name. Nothing more.
monday.when: Monday morning, in the ten minutes before the finance meeting
monday.stop_condition: If nobody can be named as owner, or the current process takes under an hour a month, I drop it.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved any AI tool for finance data, and the module said nothing on cost or GDPR.

misconception.why: I came in thinking AI is a licence you buy. The module's point that access is a switch and absorption happens in people's weeks, with someone answerable, matches what I saw in the failed programmes. I still don't believe it is a capability we build until I see a figure for it.

one_line: It has a good point about licences versus actual use and about naming an owner, but there was no cost, no payback and no number all day.
